subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw adopt Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 as its first supported third-party capture contract, and what durable provenance and collection-completeness semantics must be stored and backed up?
rationale: Source inspection establishes architectural fit but cannot determine which external producer becomes a supported compatibility contract or how its ambiguous account and collection semantics should become durable product behavior.

options.title: Start with Scrollmark v1
options.body: Approve only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle initially, define durable provenance and partial-membership semantics, and evaluate other exporters after that contract is proven.

options.title: Support multiple exporters now
options.body: Approve Scrollmark plus legacy and twitter-web-exporter formats together, accepting a larger normalization, fixture, migration, and compatibility surface for the first implementation.

options.title: Defer third-party imports
options.body: Keep official archives, Birdclaw backups, and live transports as the only supported ingestion sources until the external formats mature further.

recommendation.title: Start with Scrollmark v1
recommendation.body: Approve only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle initially, define durable provenance and partial-membership semantics, and evaluate other exporters after that contract is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the repository vision, durable schema, canonical entity semantics, and long-term supported-source contract connected to their recent work.
